1.why: All MFA endpoints go through auth() and operate only on the single session-bound account; user/account identifiers in input are rejected via suppliedIdentifier().

2.why: Verification uses account.pending/secret for the authenticated session only; there is no path for one user’s OTP to authenticate as another user.

3.why: Enabling MFA in /api/mfa/verify sets account.enabled but does not invalidate or rotate existing entries in the sessions Map, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: Pending/OTP secret is stored via AES-GCM encrypt(); recovery codes store SHA-256 hashes plus AES-GCM ciphertext, not plaintext.

5.why: Secrets, session tokens, CSRF values, and recovery codes are produced with crypto.getRandomValues (and base32/recovery helpers built on it).

6.why: bank_session is Set-Cookie with HttpOnly; no code writes secrets/OTPs/session tokens to localStorage, sessionStorage, or non-HttpOnly cookies.

7.why: Server validates email (emailOK), phone (phoneOK), OTP (/^\d{6}$/), recovery format, JSON shape/size, and rejects unexpected identifier fields.

8.why: Client esc() uses textContent before innerHTML; CSP script-src/style-src are nonce-based, limiting XSS even if markup slipped through.

9.why: No server-side redirect endpoints exist; navigation is client hash-only, so open redirects are not possible.

10.why: headers() sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options DENY, and frame-ancestors 'none' on responses.

11.why: Login Set-Cookie includes HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict (and logout clears with the same flags).

12.why: API errors are generic with no stack traces and secrets are not put in URLs; however the client deliberately console/logs panel-prints secrets and recovery codes during enrolment.

13.why: Pending OTP has expires (OTP_LIFE) and used flag; TOTP is step-windowed; recovery codes are marked used after redeem.

14.why: Failed OTP verify locks pending after 5 attempts for LOCK; recovery redeem similarly rate-limits via failures/recoveryLocked.

15.why: Login issues a new session token and deletes the prior cookie session; IDLE/ABSOLUTE timeouts are enforced in auth(); logout deletes the session and clears the cookie.
